title: Roman and neighboring polity boundaries
time_resolution: dated intervals rendered on an annual timeline
notes: Each geometry persists from FromYear through ToYear. Annual playback is display interpolation, not an annual observation. Geometry is simplified for web display.

title: Published and explicit Roman force estimates
time_resolution: seven irregular, non-interpolated estimates in four separately defined segments
notes: Only an ancient reported deployment, one explicit unit model, and published modern estimates remain. Lines connect points only when polity, scope, and estimation family are comparable. No western fifth-century total is plotted because the current evidence audit did not find a defensible published establishment estimate.

title: Reported and reconstructed rival campaign forces
time_resolution: dated campaign observations only
notes: Each row is one reported, reconstructed, or modern-minimum campaign force. The dataset deliberately contains no interpolated state-capacity series.

title: Republican Roman worked-metal comparison
time_resolution: third and second centuries BCE only
notes: Relative index with the nearest comparator normalized to 100. The public source supports the 25% comparison but not absolute kilograms for every army.

title: Physical and geographic basemap
time_resolution: not historical
notes: Modern coastlines, rivers, and borders provide orientation only and are not evidence for ancient political boundaries.

title: Reconstructed Roman imperial budget scenarios
time_resolution: two snapshots, c. 150 and c. 215 CE, each with low and high scenarios
notes: Duncan-Jones's central-expenditure reconstruction as reproduced by Mattingly. Categories sum within each published scenario. Nominal totals across the two dates are not presented as real growth.

title: Roman fiscal rates, transfers, grain, and legionary pay
time_resolution: irregular dated observations from 123 BCE to 197 CE
notes: Each rate retains its own payer, base, geography, destination, and unit. The values are not combined into an empire-wide tax rate or a purchasing-power series.

title: Selected western Roman fiscal-political shocks and recoveries
time_resolution: twelve selected dated events from 395 to 476 CE
notes: A selective chronology of interacting political, military, territorial, and fiscal changes. Event markers are not causal scores and do not imply a continuous decline.

title: Heather's African revenue-loss military equivalents
time_resolution: two regional components after the fifth-century African losses
notes: Published fiscal equivalents using Elton's annual maintenance costs. Values are not observed troop reductions or a western army census; the Proconsularis–Byzacena cavalry value is a lower bound.

title: Roman institutional afterlives on different clocks
time_resolution: irregular milestones from 312 BCE to 1453 CE plus three road-network summary measures
notes: Four parallel trajectories—roads, language, law, and the eastern Roman state—retain unlike evidence types and explicit limits. They are not combined into a legacy score.

title: Proto-cuneiform archive composition and CDLI corpus snapshot
time_resolution: Uruk IV and III phase summaries plus a corpus snapshot dated 19 May 2020
notes: Published bounded genre shares and corpus-filter counts. Values describe surviving, cataloged, transliterated material—not ancient production or a census of writing.

title: Uruk urbanization evidence clocks and settlement footprints
time_resolution: five irregular chronology intervals and five phase-level settlement-footprint observations from 4400 to 2900 BCE
notes: Urban scale, public institutions, record-keeping, and political interpretation remain separate evidence lanes. Settlement hectares are not converted into population, and no annual growth or state-birth threshold is interpolated.

title: Southern Mesopotamian water-ecology evidence and preserved canal-network summary
time_resolution: irregular proxy and evidence intervals from 9700 to 1000 BCE plus one explicitly undated mixed-age palaeochannel layer
notes: Local borehole evidence, regional climate synthesis, Uruk's urban interval, later directly dated canals, textual evidence, and the multi-period Eridu network remain distinct. The palaeochannel map is not a fourth-millennium time slice, and the canal counts are not simultaneous.

title: Competing evidence for cereal appropriability and Uruk's mixed resource economy
time_resolution: five qualitative resource comparisons plus five claim-test observations spanning direct Late Uruk evidence global comparative studies and an explicitly later Ur III methodological comparison
notes: No numeric legibility or causal score is computed. The original global model, its 2026 published challenge, direct Late Uruk records, regional deltaic ecology, and later evidence of institutional archive bias remain separate. Archive visibility is not treated as dietary or economic share.

title: Archaeological evidence for early-state concentration reversibility and incomplete control
time_resolution: eight irregular site and regional observations from approximately 4200 to 3100 BCE
notes: Unlike observations retain their original units and inference limits. Counts are not added or converted into a fragility score; bowls do not establish slavery, walls do not measure coercion, abandonment is not a death count, and no Uruk disease series is inferred.

title: Urban scale, political centralization, and durable-notation evidence clocks across six regions
time_resolution: eighteen region-clock observations: seventeen phase ranges or dated contexts and one explicitly undated Andean notation gap
notes: The six-region frame is a debated comparative device, not a canonical list or rank. Urban scale, political centralization, and durable notation remain separate clocks. Dates are not annual series or confidence intervals; the Andean notation gap is not plotted at year zero.

title: Water rainfall crops transport and settlement-form profiles across six early urban regions
time_resolution: thirty region-dimension observations with source-specific places and phase or synthesis windows
notes: The six-by-five matrix computes no hydraulic, aridity, productivity, legibility, density, or state-causation score. Every cell preserves its evidence class and inference limit. Settlement form replaces a numeric density comparison because survey coverage, preservation, phase length, and population models are not commensurable.

title: Cities states notation monumental building and bronze evidence clocks across six regions
time_resolution: thirty region-milestone observations from 4000 BCE to 1521 CE including one explicitly undated Andean notation gap
notes: The existing city state and notation clocks are reused without changing their evidence status. Monument and bronze rows preserve regional thresholds: rare attestation sustained use analytical assemblage or regional scaling. Ordinal order is derived only from phase starts; bronze is not treated as a civilization score or prerequisite and the Andean notation gap is not plotted at year zero.

title: Institutional routes from resources and labor to coordinated action across six early urban regions
time_resolution: twenty-four unlike site phase regional and textual observations grouped as four inspectable routes per region
notes: Inputs coordinators and visible outcomes form qualitative evidence chains rather than measurements. Four rows per region are an editorial sampling frame not a prevalence count. The dataset computes no surplus tax storage labor coercion diversity or state-capacity score and every row preserves its inference limit.

title: Six regional pathways after early urban or political systems changed
time_resolution: six unlike site regional and political transition cases from the fourth millennium BCE to the first millennium CE
notes: Each row distinguishes a prior system an observable transition and a bounded afterlife. The cases are not synchronized and compute no collapse resilience continuity population-loss or civilizational score. Settlement persistence does not by itself establish population institutional or political continuity.

title: Copper and tin evidence places and connections across the Bronze Age Mediterranean and Eurasia
time_resolution: nineteen evidence-place rows and sixteen bounded connections from the eighteenth through thirteenth centuries BCE
notes: Four views keep one cargo Cypriot copper distribution Atlantic tin compatibility and a textual exchange relationship separate. Connections are evidence links not reconstructed routes. The dataset contains no annual trade volumes traffic estimates market shares or inferred direct voyages and preserves competing Uluburun tin-source claims.

title: Five selectively visible institutional circuits at Bronze Age palace centers
time_resolution: five unlike case windows from the early eighteenth through late thirteenth centuries BCE
notes: Each row follows one unusually visible resource or information circuit through an institutional aperture and keeps its outside-palace limit attached. Archive counts sheep tallies metal allotments and one silo episode retain unlike units and are never summed ranked or converted into a centralization or state-capacity score.

title: Five evidence windows onto Bronze Age chariot horses vehicles people upkeep and institutions
time_resolution: five unlike case windows from the fifteenth century BCE through the late Shang period
notes: The comparison preserves six dependencies without scoring completeness or effectiveness. Husiatyn lacks a vehicle; Kikkuli's at-least-184-day schedule is reconstructed; Pylian wheels are not complete chariots; EA 15 is a diplomatic gift; and Anyang mortuary contexts are not field organization.

title: Three shipwreck and two harbor windows onto plural Bronze Age maritime exchange
time_resolution: five unlike evidence windows and nineteen bounded associations from the seventeenth through twelfth centuries BCE
notes: Uluburun Cape Gelidonya Point Iria Kommos and Hala Sultan Tekke remain unlike cargo and harbor records. Connections identify material analytical or typological associations rather than direct voyages annual traffic market shares ownership or one unified trade institution.

title: Six unlike windows onto Late Bronze Age destruction contraction survival and reorganization
time_resolution: six non-synchronous windows from approximately 1250 to 1100 BCE including one explicitly comparative regional frame
notes: Environmental context conflict testimony institutional change and persistence remain prose evidence rather than additive variables. Date bands are orientation windows not annual measurements or uncertainty distributions. No shared collapse year cause score resilience score population loss or common attacker is inferred.

title: Five regional windows separating first iron evidence from wider adoption
time_resolution: five broad regional phase windows from the early second millennium through 500 BCE
notes: First evidence and wider adoption are separate synthesis windows. Five production dependencies remain prose evidence rather than scores. The dataset does not estimate annual output market share diffusion speed hardness fuel efficiency military power or a universal Iron Age threshold.

title: Eleven measured modern bloomery experiments from Meroe and Sehnde reconstruction programs
time_resolution: individual modern experimental runs rather than a historical time series
notes: Ore charcoal and reported bloom masses stay at run level. Charcoal per kilogram of bloom is a transparent derived ratio. Zero and trace outputs remain categories; the data do not estimate ancient output woodland loss labor weapon totals or civilization-level efficiency.

title: Paired bloom and forged-bar metallography from four controlled smelting experiments
time_resolution: eight samples from four modern experimental runs rather than a historical series
notes: Hardness means sample counts standard deviations chemistry microstructure and forgeability remain distinct. The dataset does not convert hardness into toughness weapon performance service life battlefield effect or a material-superiority score.

title: Four bounded cases separating equipment access from recruitment supply and replacement
time_resolution: one Bronze Age campaign structure one broad pre-Roman transition and two same-model Punic War strategic maxima
notes: Only the Carthaginian and Roman values share a model family and receive proportional bars. Kadesh remains a campaign inference and the pre-Roman civitas case has no headcount. The dataset contains no kilograms per soldier artifact-derived army total replacement curve causal share or military-power score.

title: Five bounded iron-production architectures from household networks to royal and state systems
time_resolution: five unlike institutional cases from the ninth century BCE through the fifth century CE
notes: Inputs making coordination distribution and visible evidence remain separate. The rows do not calculate output centralization market integration state capacity productivity labor totals or a universal development sequence.

title: Herodotus's Sardis–Susa itinerary and four bounded road-and-relay evidence classes
time_resolution: six itinerary segments and four source-bounded evidence windows from 509 to 480 BCE and mid-fifth-century reporting
notes: The itinerary preserves stages and parasangs without kilometre conversion. Ninety days is Herodotus's arithmetic; the relay description has no end-to-end duration; the Persepolis archive is regional. No imperial-speed score route geometry traffic estimate or universal travel model is produced.
